channel.title: Wisconsin Newspaper Association - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from Wisconsin Newspaper Association (wnanews.com)

item.title: WNA Foundation announces 2025 high school student contest winners
item.description: The WNA Foundation on Thursday, March 5 celebrated Wisconsin’s outstanding student journalists, announcing the winners of its 2025 high school Better Newspaper Contest during the Branen Family Student Luncheon held as part of the 2026 WNA Convention at the Madison Concourse Hotel in Madison.

item.title: WNA Foundation announces 2025 collegiate student contest winners
item.description: The WNA Foundation on Thursday, March 5 celebrated Wisconsin’s outstanding student journalists, announcing the winners of its 2025 collegiate Better Newspaper Contest during the Branen Family Student Luncheon held as part of the 2026 WNA Convention at the Madison Concourse Hotel in Madison.

item.title: WNA testifies against AB 1034/SB 1075 Public Records exemption
item.description: Wisconsin Newspaper Association Executive Director Beth Bennett testified last week at the Wisconsin State Capitol against Assembly Bill 1034/Senate Bill 1075, also known to many as the Name Image and Likeness Bill, that provide debt relief for existing University of Wisconsin athletic facilities.

item.title: Lakeland Times, Wisconsin State Journal named 2025 Newspapers of the Year
item.description: The Wisconsin Newspaper Association honored the work of newspapers across the state during its 2025 Better Newspaper Contest Awards Luncheon on Friday, March 6, 2026 at The Madison Concourse Hotel in downtown Madison, Wisconsin.

item.title: No stopping the press for Simpson Street kids
item.description: Thanks to a recent six-figure grant from a local service organization, Simpson Street Free Press -- staffed by Madison area students -- will be able to continue literary exploration.

item.title: You can’t change time
item.description: Biannually I am somewhat miffed that it feels like an hour of my life has been arbitrarily changed by a political rule where we want to mess with the natural rhythm of nature.

item.title: Opees highlight good works, and bad
item.description: In advance of national Sunshine Week (sunshineweek.org), March 15-21, the Wisconsin Freedom of Information Council has named the winners of its 20th annual Openness in Government Awards, or Opees.

item.title: Wisconsin Freedom of Information Council names ‘Opee’ winners
item.description: Two attempts to peel back the veil of secrecy over the proliferation of data centers are being honored in this year’s Openness in Government Awards, or Opees, bestowed by the Wisconsin Freedom of Information Council.

item.title: Runberg writes final column for Free Press
item.description: Editor Justin Runberg published his final column in the March 3, 2026 issue of the Amery Free Press.

item.title: Gruich fires attorney in case that included threat against Wisconsin newspaper publisher
item.description: A Michigan man accused of threatening an Oneida County judge and newspaper publisher Gregg Walker has dismissed his attorney and retained new legal counsel, prompting the court to postpone his upcoming jury trial and schedule a new trial date.
